card.change: Refine scored parent attempt 3 with one controlled modelling change. Replace LightGBM objective=lambdarank, metric=ndcg@5, truncation_level=8, and user-query chunking with objective=binary and chronological holdout metric=AUC; every training row now contributes pointwise log-loss gradients. Keep the same 63-leaf tree capacity, learning rate, 240-round ceiling, 30-round early stopping, last-three-date chronological split, split-specific and full-data smoothed tables, leave-one-row-out training encodings, metadata parsing, feature order, unknown handling, source-row restoration, and checkpoint-only final inference. Refit the frozen binary booster on all training dates for the selected round count, save the unchanged aggregate tables plus the booster and manifest, and generate attempt predictions by reloading that checkpoint through the final inference path.
evidence: STATE:attempt 3 is the first scored candidate and passed checkpoint replay, but returned GAUC=0.4391458020855132, nDCG@5=0.46472532822498236, and primary=0.4519355651552478. The 0.02558 nDCG-over-GAUC gap is the measured outcome this objective change targets; there is no remaining execution error to debug.

STATE:attempt 3 selected only 25 LambdaRank rounds on its chronological holdout (reported holdout nDCG@5=0.362738), so simply adding more trees under the same top-truncated selection rule is lower value than changing the loss while preserving the learned feature family.

EDA:user-history-density-and-support reports a median 3,489 rows per user, p90 11,662, and maximum 49,242. LambdaRank truncation level 8 therefore directly emphasizes a tiny fraction of each query, whereas GAUC depends on ordering positives and negatives throughout eligible users.

Guidance:ORGANIZER_REFERENCE states that GAUC excludes degenerate users, weights eligible users by positive count, and uses average ranks for ties, while the campaign primary weights GAUC and nDCG@5 equally. An all-row binary objective is a direct test of the broad-ordering half that attempt 3 missed.

Source:LightGBM official LambdaRank documentation, as recorded in the accepted research plan, supports truncation near the desired nDCG cutoff but explicitly does not establish an advantage for this campaign's equal GAUC/nDCG mean; the accepted plan predeclared abandoning LambdaRank if pointwise learning improves primary.

Feedback:research_plan_review says to prefer GAUC-improving changes when metrics conflict, and Feedback:candidate-review-1788212895844887351 makes the simpler supervised/objective comparison mandatory after the bundled first viable model.

EDA:tab-context-distribution, EDA:duration-scale-and-outliers, EDA:user-history-density-and-support, EDA:validation-cold-item-rate, and EDA:metadata-coverage-and-shape still support the parent feature set, so those inputs are deliberately held fixed to isolate the objective mechanism.
STATE:attempt 1 established that evaluation_features lacks play_time_ms, so deterministic target reconstruction remains unexecutable and cannot supersede this learned refinement.
card.falsifier: Reject executability if checkpoint-only replay on the same label-free data_root differs from attempt predictions within controller tolerance or if predictions are not one finite score per authoritative input row. Reject the all-row pointwise-objective hypothesis if controller primary does not exceed attempt 3's 0.4519355651552478 by the campaign's frozen epsilon. In particular, if GAUC fails to improve materially over 0.4391458020855132, broad pair ordering was not primarily limited by top-truncated LambdaRank; if GAUC rises but a compensating nDCG@5 loss prevents an epsilon primary gain, retain both checkpoints only as parents for a separately frozen ensemble experiment rather than declaring this refinement sufficient.
card.hypothesis: Attempt 3's LambdaRank objective concentrated learning on approximately the top eight positions inside user queries containing thousands of impressions. That emphasis can improve the first five ranks while leaving most positive-negative pairs poorly ordered, which is consistent with the observed nDCG@5 of 0.4647253282 but sub-random GAUC of 0.4391458021. Holding the entire feature and preprocessing pipeline fixed while fitting pointwise binary loss and selecting rounds by chronological AUC should use every labelled row, improve the broad within-user ordering measured by GAUC, and retain enough of the same tab, duration, user-context, and metadata signal to improve the arithmetic-mean primary.
